description: Fast-growing native elder with broad heads of cream flowers followed by small dark berries. It fills a new planting quickly while the slower trees establish.
ecology: A shrub of woodland edges and disturbed ground. Grows fast, flowers young, and produces both an insect crop and a fruit crop in its first few years.
wildlifeNotes: Birds take the dark berries readily. The wide flower heads carry a lot of insects, which is what brings the insectivorous birds in.
flowering: Broad cream flower heads in spring and summer
propagation: Very easy from cuttings, and fast from seed.
medicinalUses: The flowers are taken as an infusion for fever and colds, a long-standing use across the region.
safety: The flowers are the part used. Raw berries and the green parts upset the stomach.
